title: Phones and power
steps: Download offline Google Maps areas for Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka and Hong Kong.
Save flight, hotel and the main booking confirmations offline.
Screenshot each hotel name and address in the local script, from the booking confirmation, to show a driver if a phone dies or data misbehaves.
sequence MIYASHITA PARK, Shibuya: 東京都渋谷区神宮前6-20-10 MIYASHITA PARK North.
sequence KYOTO GOJO: 京都府京都市下京区五条烏丸町409.
THE BLOSSOM HIBIYA, Tokyo: 東京都港区新橋1-1-13.
Sheraton Hong Kong, 香港喜來登酒店: 九龍尖沙咀彌敦道20號.
A power bank and a USB-C cable each. Every night, charge phones, power banks and AirPods.
Keep one phone able to receive Australian SMS for banking and two-factor codes.

title: eSIM and wifi
steps: Ubigi Best Asia Unlimited, 15 days, AU$78 each. One for each phone. The 15 days run to the evening of Sat 31, covering the flight home.
Install both eSIMs at home on wifi, then leave the Ubigi line switched off. Best Asia stays waiting to start, so nothing is used.
On landing in Hong Kong, Fri 16 at 21:45: Settings, Mobile, Ubigi line, turn it on. Ubigi Data Roaming on. Mobile Data set to Ubigi.
Australian SIM: Data Roaming off, but keep the line on for SMS and two-factor codes. The Ubigi app should then show the plan as active.
Covers Japan (KDDI, Docomo) and Hong Kong (Smartone) with no change. 30GB at full speed, then 2 Mbps; track it in the Ubigi app, top up there if needed.
Phone settings: Auto-Join on for hotel wifi, Wi-Fi Assist off, photo backup on wifi only.

title: Suica and Octopus
steps: Both are already in your Apple Wallets. Tap the phone at the gate, no need to unlock it with Express Mode on.
Top up in Wallet with Apple Pay. Keep about ¥2,000 on Suica.
Suica works on trains, metros and buses across Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka, and at convenience stores, lockers and vending machines.
It does not pay for Shinkansen or Narita Express tickets.
Octopus does the same job in Hong Kong: MTR, Star Ferry, trams, buses and convenience stores.
Spend the Suica balance airside at Haneda.

title: Tax-free shopping
steps: Take the physical passports. The shop scans the entry sticker. A photo is not accepted.
Spend ¥5,000 or more before tax in one store on the same day. Food and other goods can be added together to reach it. Look for the Tax-Free sign, or the tax-free counter in a department store.
Prices already include Japan's tax. Tax-free means it isn't charged: 10% on most goods and alcohol, 8% on take-away food and soft drinks. That is about 9% and 7% off the shelf price.
Restaurant meals are never tax-free. Department stores refund at a separate counter, less about 1.5%.
Food, drinks and cosmetics are sealed in a bag. Keep it sealed until you leave Japan.
Tax-free QR, at home: in Visit Japan Web, personal details, turn on "Use tax-free QR code" and scan both passports with the phone camera.

Tax-free QR, at Narita: immigration sticks a landing permission sticker with a QR in each passport. Check you both get one. Then in Visit Japan Web open the tax-free section, scan each sticker, and the QR is ready. Show it live at the till; carry passports anyway.
Back in Australia: AUD 900 of goods, 2.25 L of alcohol and 25 cigarettes each. Declare all food and wood. Undeclared items risk a fine of about AUD 626.
This at-the-till system runs to 31 October, so it covers the trip. It changes on 1 November.

title: Narita Express ticket, Sat 17
steps: After customs, follow the signs for Railways down to the basement level.
Buy at the JR East Travel Service Centre or a JR ticket machine with the N'EX logo. Every seat is reserved, so the ticket gives you a car and seat. No need to book from home.
Ask for Shibuya. Check the train on your ticket stops at Shibuya, as not every service does.
About 75 to 80 minutes. Big bags go in the racks at the end of the car.
Pay by card. Suica does not cover the express fare.

title: Shibuya Station to the hotel, Sat 17
steps: Leave by the Hachikō exit, the one for the dog statue and the Scramble Crossing.
Keep the rail line on your right and walk north along it to Miyashita Park, the long building with the park on its roof.
Sequence Miyashita Park is the tower at the far, northern end. About 7 minutes, flat.
Take the lift to the lobby on the 4th floor. Leave the bags and ask about early check-in.

title: Shibuya Sky, what to leave behind
steps: Not allowed on the rooftop: bags, backpacks and pouches, hats and caps, tripods and selfie sticks, earbuds and headphones, food and drink, and anything loose that could blow away.
Fine to take: a phone, and a camera on a strap.
Everything else goes into the free lockers on the 46th floor, which means a queue on the way in and again on the way out.
So drop it all at the hotel first, seven minutes away. Wear pockets that close. Take phones, the booking QR code and one card.

title: Moving teamLab for wet weather
steps: Booked for Mon 26 at 08:30. The date or time can be changed up to three times.
Open the booking from the confirmation email and choose the change option.
Good places for it: any wet morning on the Shibuya leg, or Sunday 25 morning in place of the gardens.
From Shibuya it is about 30 minutes by metro to Azabudai Hills, or 15 to 20 minutes by taxi.
If it moves, Monday 26 starts in Asakusa about 10:00.

title: Omotesando and Aoyama store hours, Sun 18
steps: Checked for Sunday 18: AMORE Omotesando 10:00 to 21:00, AMORE Vintage Aoyama 10:00 to 20:00, QOO 11:30 to 20:00, Brand Collect (both shops) 11:00 to 19:00, ALLU 11:00 to 20:00, Casanova Vintage 12:00 to 20:00.
All within a few minutes of Omotesando Hills. Brand Collect is known for the best Chanel prices, ALLU for Hermès.
Weekend afternoons are busy: go straight to the pieces you want. Physical passports for tax-free.
Back to the hotel: a 10 minute taxi from Omotesando, or 20 minutes on foot down Cat Street.

title: G on his own, Sun 18
steps: ZARA Harajuku is closed. Use ZARA Shibuya Kōen-dōri instead, 1-22-4 Jinnan, 10:30 to 22:00.
Walk down Cat Street from Omotesando into Jinnan, about 15 minutes.
First stop: Mominotakumi, 9F, same block as ZARA and Ichiran. Book two foot massages for about 19:45 tonight. Open to 23:00, +81 3-6416-0995.
ZARA Kōen-dōri for cargo pants, four floors.
Nintendo Tokyo, Shibuya Parco 6F, 3 minutes away, 10:00 to 21:00. The Pokémon Center and Capcom Store share the floor.
H&M Udagawachō, beside MEGA Don Quijote, 10:00 to 22:00. Menswear is on 4F.
H&M to the hotel is about 8 minutes on foot. Back by 14:20.

title: Omoide Yokochō, Tue 20
steps: Memory Lane: two narrow alleys beside the west exit of Shinjuku Station, with about 60 tiny yakitori counters and bars under red lanterns.
Arrive about 17:30. By 19:00 the popular counters are full.
Pick any counter with two free seats. Order a drink each and a few skewers, then move on. Two or three places is the normal way to do it.
Many counters add a small seating charge, a few hundred yen each, and bring a small snack you did not order. It is called otoshi (お通し): that is the charge, so it is normal, not a mistake.
Check the menu and prices before you sit. If none are posted, ask, or pick a counter that shows them. Counters are tiny and best for two.
Carry cash. Some counters do not take cards.
It is smoky from the grills, and some counters allow smoking.
This is the place to eat. Golden Gai, later, is tiny bars for drinking.
Golden Gai, about 20:00: around 200 tiny bars across six alleys. Look for an English menu or sign on the door, which means visitors are welcome.
Some bars are for locals or regulars only. If the sign or the barman says so, move on.
Take cash. Most bars charge a cover of roughly ¥500 to ¥1,500 each before the first drink, usually posted at the door.
Many bars do not allow photos inside, and some lanes ask for none at all.
Kabukichō on the way: ignore touts, and never follow anyone off the street into a bar.

title: Hotel to the Shinkansen, Wed 21
steps: The night before: pack, settle the bill, and ask the front desk to book a taxi for 06:30.
05:55 wake. 06:20 check out. 06:30 taxi to Shinagawa Station, Kōnan exit, which is the Shinkansen side. About 20 to 25 minutes.
About 07:00 at Shinagawa. Buy ekiben and coffee inside the Shinkansen gates.
On the platform by 07:40. Nozomi 13 leaves at 07:55. Car 9, seats 16-C and 16-D. Bags go in the oversized baggage space behind the last row.
Fallback if no taxi comes: JR Yamanote line from Shibuya to Shinagawa, about 13 minutes, leaving by 06:45.

title: Kyoto Station, bags and the walk, Wed 21
steps: Use Crosta Kyoto, the staffed baggage counter on level B1, directly below the JR Central Gate on the north, Kyoto Tower side. Open 08:00 to 20:00. ¥1,000 per bag per day. Not the Hachijō gate counter by the Shinkansen, which shuts at 18:00.

Before the bags go over the counter, take out: passports, wallets and cards, phones, chargers and power bank, medication, a warm layer, and anything valuable or fragile. Valuables are not accepted in stored bags.

From the Nozomi at 10:00: go out through the Shinkansen gates and follow the signs for the Central Gate and the Karasuma side, along the upper walkway across the tracks. About 7 minutes with the bags.
At the Central Gate, take the escalator down to B1. The counter is behind the escalators, signed for baggage. Hand the bags over, pay, and keep the receipt. You need it to collect.
For Nara: back up the escalator and through the station's central passage to the Kintetsu gates on the south side, about 10 minutes (How-to 24).
Coming back about 17:25: out through the Central Gate, down to B1, collect with the receipt. With a 20:00 close, a late train is not a problem.
Option: Crosta delivers to Kyoto hotels for ¥1,500 a bag if dropped by 14:00. Ask the hotel first.

To sequence KYOTO GOJO: out the north side, the Kyoto Tower side, then straight north up Karasuma-dōri to Gojō. About 15 minutes, flat. Or take the Karasuma subway line one stop to Gojō, then walk 3 minutes. Or a taxi from the north rank.

title: Osaka there and back, Thu 22
steps: Out: one subway stop from Gojō to Kyoto Station, or a 15 minute walk. Leave the hotel at 07:00.
JR special rapid from Kyoto to Osaka Station, about 30 minutes. They run every 15 minutes and Suica works. No seat booking.
At Osaka, change to the JR Osaka Loop Line, outer loop, to Osakajōkōen. About 10 minutes. The castle park is at the exit.
After the castle, walk to Tanimachi 4-chōme on its west side and buy the Enjoy Eco Card day pass at the metro ticket machine. About ¥820 on a weekday. It covers the Osaka Metro, not JR.
Back: Midōsuji line from Namba to Umeda, four stops. Walk through to JR Osaka Station.
JR special rapid to Kyoto, about 30 minutes. Then the subway one stop to Gojō, or walk.
Leaving Namba at 21:30 puts you home about 22:45. The last trains are after 23:30, but check the night before.

title: Dōtonbori canal boat, Thu 22
steps: The Tombori River Cruise leaves from the canal beside the Don Quijote building.
Buy tickets at the booth when you arrive in Dōtonbori at 18:30, for a boat after dark. They sell by time slot.
About 20 minutes on the water under the neon.
The Glico Running Man photo platform is at the Nanohana cosmetics shop, directly opposite the sign.
Times and price not yet checked. Skip it without regret if the queue is long.

title: Kyoto back to Tokyo, Sat 24
steps: Check out and leave the hotel at 10:30. Walk straight down Karasuma-dōri, about 15 minutes, or take the subway one stop.
11:15 at Kyoto Station. Ekiben and coffee, then through the Shinkansen gates.
Nozomi 16 leaves at 12:01. Car 9, seats 1-C and 1-D. Fuji is on the left.
14:15 Tokyo Station. Follow the Yaesu exit signs to the taxi rank. Ten to fifteen minutes to the Blossom.

title: Laundry, if needed
steps: Done in Kyoto on Fri 23, so not needed in Tokyo. Kept for reference.
By Sunday 25 you are a week in. Three good slots: Friday 23 evening in Kyoto, Sunday 25 morning at the Blossom, which is the easiest, or Monday 26 before dinner.
The Blossom has a guest laundry with only a few machines, so go early. Not confirmed for sequence KYOTO GOJO, so ask at check-in there.
A wash and dry takes about 90 minutes and a few hundred yen. Have ¥100 coins ready.
No machines, or all busy: ask the desk for the nearest coin laundry.
Hotel laundry service is charged per item and usually has to be handed in by mid morning for same-day return. Worth it for a few pieces only.
Last chance: the Sheraton in Hong Kong, by laundry service.

title: Taxi or train to Haneda, Tue 27
steps: Plan: taxi from the hotel at 06:40, booked at the front desk on Monday. About 20 to 25 minutes. Ask for the flat fare (定額運賃), about ¥5,900 from Minato ward plus tolls.
Driver phrase: 羽田空港 第3ターミナル 出発ロビーまでお願いします。 (Haneda Terminal 3, departures, please.)
If the taxi does not show by 06:50, take the train:
Monday night: pack, settle the bill, and check the first trains in the maps app.
05:45 wake. 06:22 leave the hotel and walk to Shimbashi Station, about 8 minutes. Go down to the Toei Asakusa line, platform 1.
06:38 Airport Rapid Limited Express, direct to Haneda Airport Terminal 3. About 25 minutes. Suica works.
Backup: the 06:45 Express, also direct.
Do not board a train bound for Nishi-magome. It does not go to the airport.
If anything looks wrong, take a taxi from the hotel rank. About 25 minutes.

title: Peak Tram
steps: Book a standard one-way ticket up, for about 15:45 on Thu 29 (Plan B). The Peak Tram is not stopped by wind. Klook Fast Track runs Friday to Sunday only.
The lower terminus is on Garden Road in Central, 15 minutes uphill from the ferry or a short taxi. Sit on the right going up.
At the top, walk Lugard Road, about 20 minutes each way, for the best free view. Stay through sunset at 17:50.
Taxi down from the rank by the Peak Galleria. Tram seats face backwards on the way down.

title: Ngong Ping 360 voucher
steps: Buy two Crystal cabin vouchers on Klook before flying. Non-refundable, but good on any day up to 31 October. If wind closes it, the voucher moves to another day.
Pick the day from the forecast the night before. Clear and calm is what you want.
MTR to Tung Chung, about 50 minutes from Tsim Sha Tsui with one change. The cable car terminal is a few minutes from exit B.
Be there for the first car at 10:00. Follow the signs for Klook or prepaid vouchers, and join the Crystal cabin queue.

title: Massage near each hotel
steps: Head spas are small, appointment-only salons: book a day or two ahead. Body and foot places mostly take walk-ins. Hours from Google, October 2026; check on the day.

Shibuya. Head spa: The Head Spa Tokyo Harajuku, about 5 minutes north of the hotel, or Head Spa Josho in Omotesando, open to 22:00. Body and foot: Body Spa Sora, east side of the station, to 23:00, or Joyful Massage Spa Shibuya, open 24 hours.

Kyoto. Head spa: Head Spa Salon QUATRE near Shijō-Karasuma, one subway stop north, or The Head Spa Tokyo Kyoto at Shijō-Kawaramachi. Body and foot: YUMEMISHI Shijō-Karasuma, the closest, to 21:00, or Hannari near Nishiki, to 22:00.
Hibiya and Ginza. Head spa: Head Spa ZEN, to 23:00, or Head Spa zwei HAUS, to 22:00. Body and foot: Buasai Ginza, Thai massage 5 minutes from the hotel, to midnight, or YURAGI, to midnight.
Hong Kong. Head: Kungfu head therapy at 27 Nathan Road, two minutes from the Sheraton. Foot: Foot Lam Moon on Hankow Road, to 00:30. Body and foot: Fu Ying Massage on Granville Road, open 24 hours.

title: Footbaths in Yokohama, Mon 19 ideas
steps: Ideas, not bookings. The easy one, on the dusk walk: The Wharf House footbath terrace in Yamashita Park. Feet only.
The Wharf House: ¥300 each for 30 minutes, towel ¥200. Take a number inside, often a 20 minute wait. Closed in rain. Harbour and Bay Bridge view; the Ferris wheel is faint.
For the Ferris wheel view: Manyo Club, five minutes from the Air Cabin, has a rooftop footbath facing the wheel. Entry covers the whole spa, ¥3,600 each, in their robe.

Manyo Club risk: tattoos are refused, apart from small ones under their stickers, up to 11 cm square. The robe covers it on the roof, but not in the shared locker room. If noticed, expect to be asked to leave, no refund.

Ask Manyo Club first: call 0570-07-4126, or ask the hotel front desk to ring. Show them: 背中にタトゥーがあります。館内着で完全に隠れます。屋上の足湯だけ利用したいのですが、入館できますか？ (I have a tattoo on my back, fully covered by the loungewear. I only want the rooftop footbath. May I enter?)

title: Daikoku car meet
steps: No longer fits: Sun 25 evening is the sumo, tantanmen and a massage. Kept for reference.
An option, not a booking. Daikoku PA, on Yokohama's Bayshore Route, is where Japanese car fans meet at night. Only reachable by car, so book a tour (Klook or the operator).
You ride in a JDM car such as an R34 Skyline, RX-7 or Supra with an English-speaking guide. Pickup from the Blossom, about 3 hours, tolls included. Start about 20:00; teamLab is 08:30 Monday.
Police can close Daikoku without notice, mostly on Friday and Saturday nights. Pick a tour that moves you to another bay spot if it is shut, and check its refund terms.

title: Kyoto to Nara and back, Wed 21
steps: Kintetsu: south side of Kyoto Station. At the machine, buy Kintetsu Nara plus a limited express (特急) seat, about ¥1,280, 35 minutes. Board one signed 奈良.
No seats: the direct express (急行), 45 minutes, ¥760 on Suica, hourly. In Nara, exit for Higashimuki.
JR alternative: Miyakoji rapid from the JR gates, 45 minutes, ¥720 on Suica, then 20 minutes on foot to the park.

title: Getting to Street Kart, Sun 18
steps: Check the voucher for the shop name. Rainbow Bridge tours run from Street Kart Tokyo Bay (Shinkiba) and the Shinagawa shop.

Tokyo Bay shop, Shinkiba, Kōtō: from Shibuya take the JR Saikyō line toward Shin-Kiba. Many trains run straight through on the Rinkai line; if not, change at Ōsaki to the Rinkai line. About 30 minutes. Suica works. Then about 10 minutes on foot from Shin-Kiba Station.
Shinagawa shop: JR Yamanote from Shibuya to Shinagawa, about 12 minutes, then the walk shown on the voucher.
Or a taxi from the hotel: 25 to 35 minutes and roughly ¥5,000 to ¥6,500 to either. Show the driver the address from the voucher.
Leave the hotel by 14:45 to be there at 15:30, 30 minutes before the start.
Take: physical driving licence cards, physical International Driving Permits, passports, fully closed shoes. No digital copies. Costumes are optional.
If it can’t run today, the backup is Sun 25 or Mon 26 from the Hibiya hotel.

title: Finding Premier Mai, Sun 18
steps: Address: 1-6-10 Tomigaya, Yoyogi Park Building, 2F. About a minute from Yoyogi-Kōen Station (Chiyoda line) and Yoyogi-Hachiman Station.
There is no sign on the street. The building looks ordinary, with an Irish pub on the ground floor.
The entrance is a narrow staircase at the side of the pub. Go up to the 2nd floor. If there is a queue, it waits on those stairs: join the end.
The door at the top has no sign either. Open it and you are in.
Open 08:00 to 17:00 on Sunday, closed Wednesday. No booking. Order the thick toast or the omelette toast, and an oat latte.
No closure notice found for today. To be sure, check the Instagram stories at @premiermai_tokyo before walking over.
i2 is the backup, 3 minutes away at 1-14-13 Tomigaya, RayQuon Okushibu 1F.

title: Kamakura on the day, Mon 19
steps: Tsukiji to Kamakura: walk about 15 minutes to JR Shimbashi Station. JR Yokosuka line (blue and cream), bound for Zushi, Kurihama or Kamakura, direct to Kamakura in about 55 minutes. Suica works.
If the next train is the Tōkaidō line (orange and green), do not take it: it skips Kamakura. Wait for the Yokosuka line.
Kamakura Station east exit: walk Wakamiya-ōji or Komachi-dōri up to Tsurugaoka Hachimangū, about 10 minutes. Back to the station along Komachi-dōri for snacks.
Enoden: from the Enoden platform on the west side of Kamakura Station, 3 stops to Hase, about 5 minutes, Suica works. Sit on the left for glimpses of the sea.
Hase-dera: 5 minutes from Hase Station, open 08:00 to 17:00, ¥400. The Great Buddha (Kōtoku-in): 5 minutes further up the road, open 08:00 to 16:45, ¥300.
Pancakes: A la Mode Kamakura, 2-7-15 Hase, about 5 minutes from Hase Station towards the sea. Open 10:00 to 18:30, closed Wednesday and Saturday.

The beach: Yuigahama is about 10 minutes downhill from Hase Station. Free, open sand, black and soft. Showers only in summer, so towels are not needed unless you paddle. Watch food: the kites (hawks) swoop.

Mt Fuji: possible on a clear day, never guaranteed, and best before midday. The best spot is Inamuragasaki, two Enoden stops past Hase, then 5 minutes to the cape park. From Yuigahama look west along the coast.
Kamakura to Yokohama: Enoden back to Kamakura, then the JR Yokosuka line to Yokohama, about 25 minutes. Change to the JR Negishi line (light blue), one stop to Sakuragichō.

title: Yokohama on the day, Mon 19
steps: Sakuragichō Station: the Air Cabin is right outside the east exit. One way ¥1,000, about 5 minutes over the water to Unga Park, beside Cosmo World. Open 10:00 to 21:00.
Cosmo World: free to walk in, pay per ride at the ticket machines. Monday 11:00 to 20:00, closed Thursdays. Cash only.

Diving Coaster Vanish: the one that dives into the pool and disappears into a tunnel. About ¥900 to ¥1,000 each. Short: the fast part is about 30 seconds. Loose items go in the lockers first, staff check pockets.
Cosmo Clock 21: the big ferris wheel, about 15 minutes round. Best at sunset, around 17:05.
Harbour walk: Red Brick Warehouses, then along Yamashita Park to Chinatown, about 30 minutes at an easy pace.

Foot massage after dinner, in Chinatown: Kyūryū SPA (Kirin Kowloon), 2F on a pedestrian lane, 10:00 to 22:00, foot bath, tea and a full 60-minute foot course, card OK. Or Kaisokukan, 10:00 to 23:00, call +81 90-9375-5588.
Japanese dry head spa: Tenkū no Ryōiki, Kannai, 10 minutes walk from Chinatown, 11:00 to 22:00, rated 4.9, couples course. Book ahead by phone +81 70-3179-7818 or online.
Home: Motomachi-Chūkagai Station (Minatomirai line) at the Chinatown end. Trains run through on the Tōkyū Tōyoko line to Shibuya, about 40 minutes on an express, no change.

title: Hotel to Tsukiji by train, Mon 19
steps: About 30 to 35 minutes door to door, about ¥210 each on Suica.
Hotel to Shibuya Station: down from the 4F lobby, south along Miyashita Park to the station, 5 to 7 minutes.

Ginza line: follow the orange G signs. The platform is up high, 3F above Meiji-dōri, so take the escalators up. Shibuya is the first stop, so every train goes your way (towards Asakusa). If the first is packed, wait 2 to 3 minutes for the next and a seat.
Ride 8 stops to Ginza (G09), about 16 minutes.
Change at Ginza to the Hibiya line: follow the grey H signs, about 5 minutes underground. Do not tap out, Suica carries through. Board towards Kita-senju.
Ride 2 stops to Tsukiji (H11), about 3 minutes. Not Tsukijishijō, which is a different line.
Take Exit 1, beside the big stone Tsukiji Hongwan-ji temple. Walk 3 minutes south along Shin-Ōhashi-dōri: the outer market lanes are on the left.
At the market: most stalls are going by 07:30. Cash. Eat where you buy, not while walking.
Afterwards: about 15 minutes west along Harumi-dōri, then left to JR Shimbashi for the Yokosuka line to Kamakura (How-to 27).

title: Getting around, Mon 19 from Hase to home
steps: A la Mode to Hase-dera, 7 minutes: walk inland up the main road (Hase-dōri) to the traffic light by Hase Station, turn left, and the gate is straight ahead at the end of the road. ¥400, open to 17:00. Go up the steps to the lookout terrace for the sea view.
Hase-dera to the Great Buddha, 7 minutes: back down to the main road, turn left (inland) and walk up it. Kōtoku-in is on the left. ¥300, last entry 16:45.
Optional Yuigahama: from the Great Buddha walk back down the main road past Hase Station to the sea, about 12 minutes. Back to Hase Station is 5 minutes.
Hase to Kamakura: Enoden from Hase Station, platform for Kamakura (鎌倉方面), 3 stops, about 5 minutes. Kamakura is the end of the line.

Kamakura Station to lunch: walk through to the JR east exit. Komachi-dōri starts at the red torii arch on the left of the plaza. Shirasu-don at Wasai Yakura, 2-7-28 Komachi, 2F, open 11:00 to 21:00, about halfway up on the left side.
Komachi-dōri to Tsurugaoka Hachimangū: walk to the far end of Komachi-dōri (about 8 minutes), turn right, and the shrine grounds are ahead. Up the big stone steps to the main hall. Free.
Hachimangū back to the station: down the central raised path (Dankazura) on Wakamiya-ōji, about 10 minutes, straight to Kamakura Station east exit.

Kamakura to Yokohama: JR Yokosuka line, platform for Yokohama and Tokyo (横浜・東京方面), about 25 minutes. At Yokohama, change to the JR Negishi line (light blue, 根岸線) towards Ōfuna or Isogo, one stop to Sakuragichō.

Air Cabin: out of Sakuragichō east exit, the cable car station is right there on the plaza. ¥1,000 one way, about 5 minutes, lands at Unga Park beside Cosmo World. If it is stopped for wind, walk 10 minutes along the Kishamichi promenade instead.
Cosmo World: Diving Coaster Vanish and the Cosmo Clock 21 ferris wheel. Buy tickets at the machines, cash only. Lockers by the coaster.

Harbour walk to Chinatown, about 30 minutes: east from Cosmo World along the Kishamichi promenade to the Red Brick Warehouses, then along the water past Ōsanbashi Pier into Yamashita Park. Leave the park at its middle and walk inland about 5 minutes into Chinatown.
Kyūryū SPA (Kirin Kowloon): Yamashitachō 148, 2F, on a pedestrian lane inside Chinatown. Open to 22:00. Ask for the 60-minute foot course with the foot bath. Backup: Kaisokukan, open to 23:00.

Home: Motomachi-Chūkagai Station (Minatomirai line) is at the Yamashita Park end of Chinatown. Any train towards Shibuya (渋谷方面), express (急行) or limited express (特急) is fastest, about 40 minutes. If it carries on past Shibuya, get off at Shibuya.
Shibuya to the hotel: the Tōyoko line platforms are deep underground. Follow signs up and out towards Miyashita Park, about 7 to 10 minutes to the hotel.

title: Kyoto Station, bags and the train to Nara, Wed 21
steps: Off the train (10:00): take the escalator down from the platform and go through the Shinkansen gates. Tap the same Suica you tapped in with, or put your tickets in. You are now on the south side of the station. Follow the signs for Central Gate (中央口) and the Karasuma side, along the upper walkway that crosses over the tracks. About 7 minutes with bags.

Drop the bags at Crosta (about 10:15): from the Central Gate take the escalator down to B1. The Crosta Kyoto baggage counter is behind the escalators, signed for baggage. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Crosta+Kyoto+baggage

Before the bags go over the counter, take out: passports, wallets and cards, phones, chargers and power bank, medication, umbrellas, and a light layer for the evening rain. Valuables are not accepted. ¥1,000 per bag, open until 20:00. Keep the receipt: you need it to collect.

Walk to the Kintetsu line (about 10:30): back up the escalator and south through the station's central passage to the Kintetsu gates (近鉄), about 10 minutes. Signs say Kintetsu Line, in red and white. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kintetsu+Kyoto+Station
Buy the ticket: at the Kintetsu machines tap English. Buy Kintetsu-Nara (近鉄奈良) with a limited express seat (特急), about ¥1,280 each, 35 minutes, reserved seats.
Check the destination on the ticket: some limited expresses go to Kashiharajingū-mae (橿原神宮前), which is not Nara. Yours must say 近鉄奈良, Kintetsu-Nara.
No seats left: take the Express (急行) to Nara on Suica instead. ¥760, about 45 minutes, no ticket needed.

Board (about 10:40): ticket through the gate, find the platform on the board, and the car and seat on the ticket. The limited express is the smart cream or red train with numbered cars. Get off at the end of the line, Kintetsu-Nara.

In Nara (about 11:15): take the exit for Higashimuki (東向), which comes straight up into the covered Higashimuki arcade. Walk through to Sanjō-dōri, then about 10 minutes east to lunch at Kamameshi Shizuka.

Coming back (about 16:45): Kintetsu limited express from Kintetsu-Nara back to Kyoto, about 35 minutes, arriving about 17:20. Walk to the Central Gate, down to B1, and collect the bags with the receipt.

To the hotel: walk about 15 minutes straight up Karasuma-dōri (exit on the Kyoto Tower side), or the Karasuma subway one stop to Gojō. In the rain with bags, a taxi from the north rank, about 5 minutes.

title: Hotel to the Shinjuku Sumo Club and back, Sun 25
steps: Booked: 17:30, 2 adults on Klook. Doors open 17:00. No entry after 17:50.
Address for a taxi driver: 新宿区大久保2-5-22 SEKISAKU ビル 2階までお願いします。
In the rain, take a taxi from the hotel door: about 25 minutes, about ¥3,500 to ¥4,000. Leave by 16:45.

Train, mostly underground: walk 5 minutes to Hibiya station and go down at the nearest entrance. Follow the underground passage east to Ginza station (signed 銀座 / Marunouchi line), about 8 minutes, all covered.
Marunouchi line (red), platform toward 新宿・荻窪. Off at 新宿三丁目 (Shinjuku-sanchōme), about 15 minutes.
Change to the Fukutoshin line (brown) toward 池袋, one stop to 東新宿 (Higashi-Shinjuku). Exit A1, about 5 minutes' walk to the club. Much less walking in the rain than from Shinjuku-sanchōme.
Back: Higashi-Shinjuku, Fukutoshin line one stop to Shinjuku-sanchōme, Marunouchi line toward 銀座・池袋 to Ginza. Then 8 minutes to Ginza Rōsokuya, or a taxi straight there: 銀座1丁目 ろうそく屋.
